clue.text: 23 awful people coming over, one with kids

indicators.note: coming over suggests turning head over heels, so the word for awful people is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: git is British slang for a contemptible person
a mother, someone with children

explanation.surface: A complaint that some dreadful people have turned up, one of them dragging children along.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 points to the answer at 23-down, MARK, which is the definition here. Git is British slang for an unpleasant person; GITS reversed gives STIG, then MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace, so the two are synonyms in the sense of a stain on reputation.

clue.text: Scrabble piece showing E, not one in the box

indicators.note: showing one letter and not another means a swap: the named letter goes in where the other one stood

parts.note: Scrabble letters are played on small tiles
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one, which is the letter swapped out

explanation.surface: A Scrabble tile turned up bearing the letter E, without a single one left in the bag.
explanation.walkthrough: In TILE the I (one) is replaced by E. The box and tele are both informal British words for television.
explanation.definitionFit: Tele is a short informal word for a television set, which British speakers also call the box.

clue.text: Wild orgies entertaining and extravagant

indicators.note: wild suggests something out of control, so the letters of the orgies are thrown into a new order
to entertain guests is to hold them within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: these six letters rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Riotous parties that are both entertaining and lavish.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' in the clue is not a link but part of the wordplay, sitting inside the rearranged orgies.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandiose means pompously showy or ambitious, which matches extravagant in the sense of overblown display.

clue.text: Wrong lighting wasting vicar's power

indicators.note: wasting means losing something, so the clergyman's word has a letter taken away

parts.note: a parson is a parish priest, like a vicar
P is the standard abbreviation for power, and is the letter removed

explanation.surface: Poor lighting in church is draining the vicar's electricity supply.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests bad illumination; the definition is a wicked act of setting fire, a wrong kind of lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property, so it is lighting a fire that is wrong.

clue.text: Funny limp only reduced left shoe

indicators.note: reduced means made smaller, so the word before it loses its final letter
funny in the sense of odd or peculiar tells us the letters that follow are arranged strangely

parts.note: the four letters rearranged
solo means alone or only; cut short it loses its last letter
L is the usual abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An odd limp caused by nothing more than a shrunken left shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLO, meaning only, is shortened to SOL. A plimsoll is the British name for a canvas gym shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A plimsoll is a light canvas sports shoe with a rubber sole, what Americans might call a sneaker.

clue.text: Christmas parcel perhaps dispatched in advance?

parts.note: the prefix meaning before or ahead of time
dispatched means sent off

explanation.surface: A Christmas parcel, perhaps mailed early to beat the holiday rush.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads the answer as PRE-SENT, sent beforehand, which is just what an early-posted gift is; 'perhaps' marks the parcel as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrapped parcel given at Christmas is a gift, and a gift is a present.

clue.text: Jaundiced addict Erica lovingly nurses

indicators.note: to nurse something is to hold it close, so the answer is cradled within the neighbouring words

parts.note: read straight through across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A patient with jaundice, a former addict, is tenderly cared for by Erica.
explanation.walkthrough: Icterus is the medical name for jaundice, so icterical is its adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Icterical is the medical adjective for jaundice, describing yellowed skin from excess bile pigment.

clue.text: Dog sprays saliva in your ear

indicators.note: something heard by your ear is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: spits means sprays saliva, and sounds the same

explanation.surface: A dog drooling all over your ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The spitz is a family of dog breeds with pointed muzzles and curled tails, such as the Pomeranian.

clue.text: Cost of 2 nice fleeces changed up to start of sale

indicators.note: taking the words only up to where an s begins means everything from that point on is left off
changed means altered, so the remaining letters are put in a different order

parts.note: these words, stopping before the final s

explanation.surface: The price of a couple of nice fleece jackets has been changed, right up until the sale begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 refers to 2-down, TELE, the television. In Britain households pay an annual TV licence fee that funds the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: The licence fee is the annual charge British households pay to legally watch television, so it is the cost of the telly.

clue.text: Chelsea net, ruining this?

indicators.note: ruining means wrecking, so the letters before it are knocked into a new arrangement

parts.note: these ten letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering what a ball in the Chelsea goal would spoil.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea is a London football club. The whole clue also defines: a ball hitting Chelsea's net spoils the goalkeeper's record of conceding nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a clean sheet is a match in which a team concedes no goals, so any goal in its net ruins it.

clue.text: Creep visiting hospital catches cold

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold onto it, so one piece ends up inside the others

parts.note: someone visiting is in, at home or at a place
C for cold, as on a tap
H for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Some unpleasant person visiting a hospital picks up a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Creep looks like a noun for an unpleasant person, but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to move forward very slowly, the same as creeping along.

clue.text: Shelter here finally protected by DM's successor

indicators.note: something protected by another is surrounded and shielded by it

parts.note: counting through two-letter codes in order, DN comes right after DM

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A refuge is found here, guarded by whoever follows a Dungeon Master or Daily Mail editor.
explanation.walkthrough: Treat DM as a letter code and step it on by one, as AA, AB, AC go: the next is DN.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is a hidden lair or retreat, a place giving shelter to an animal or person.

clue.text: Bloc on reflection regret Australia joined

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so the following word is read backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret
Oz is the informal name for Australia
joined together means at one, united

explanation.surface: A trading bloc that, thinking it over, wishes Australia had become a member.
explanation.definitionFit: The eurozone is the group of countries sharing the euro, an economic bloc of nations.

clue.text: Problem with uniform is limited identity

indicators.note: a problem is something gone wrong, so the letters with it are disordered

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dress-code problem: a uniform means a limited sense of personal identity.
explanation.definitionFit: Similitude means likeness or sameness, and identity in one sense is exact sameness between things.

clue.text: Wealthy holding company evading tax, at first glance

indicators.note: holding means keeping something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: wealthy and rich are synonyms
Co is the standard abbreviation for company

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letters of the preceding words

parts.note: the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: At first sight a rich man owns a company that dodges its taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first glance' reads as one phrase, but it splits: 'at first' takes initials and 'glance' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To ricochet is to rebound off a surface, which is what a bullet does when it glances off something.

clue.text: Writing newspaper, maybe wound player

parts.note: a person's hand is their handwriting
an organ is a publication speaking for a group

explanation.surface: Someone writing for a newspaper, perhaps about an injured sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Wound here rhymes with sound, not with tuned: the instrument is played by turning a crank.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand organ, or barrel organ, is a portable instrument played by cranking a handle, so it is a musical player that is wound.

clue.text: Meat with chilli yankee finds fair in NY

parts.note: the Spanish for meat, as in chilli con carne
Y is yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A New Yorker finds a fair selling chilli meat dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in NY' flags an American usage: carney or carny is US slang for a travelling carnival.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang carney means a carnival or travelling funfair, or someone who works at one.

clue.text: Compensation, alas for Shakespeare, pocketed by two theatres

indicators.note: something pocketed is tucked inside, so this piece sits within the others

parts.note: first theatre: a rep is a repertory theatre
ay me is an Elizabethan cry of grief used in Shakespeare's plays
second theatre: NT is the National Theatre in London

explanation.surface: Woe for Shakespeare, whose compensation was swallowed up by two playhouses.
explanation.walkthrough: Juliet sighs 'Ay me!' on her balcony. Rep (repertory theatre) and the National Theatre are the two London-style playhouses doing the pocketing.
explanation.definitionFit: Repayment is money paid back, which is a form of compensation for a loss.

clue.text: 23 that's had stuff a very long time

parts.note: to pig out, or pig, is to stuff oneself with food
an eon is an age, an immense period

explanation.surface: A mark that has been stuffed with food for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is MARK at 23-down, the victim of a con; one 'that's had' has been fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigeon is slang for a dupe, someone easily swindled, the same as a con man's mark who gets taken in.

clue.text: Lugged spring, making a piano in outhouse

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
making one thing into another means a letter is turned into a different one

parts.note: to spring is to leap
taken as written; this is the letter replaced
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
a shed is a small outbuilding

explanation.surface: Someone carried a spring into a shed, turning it into a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a piano' means the clue's a turns into the piano letter inside the spring word. Shlep is a Yiddish-derived word for haul.
explanation.definitionFit: To shlep is to carry something heavy with effort, so shlepped means lugged.

clue.text: Make longer and thinner stone cat

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds
to cat is slang for to vomit or retch

explanation.surface: How to make a fat stone cat statue longer and slimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: Cat is an old slang verb meaning to be sick. A stone is a British unit of body weight equal to 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch something is to pull it so that it becomes longer and thinner.

clue.text: Two visits to the loo, runs very bad

parts.note: first visit: crude slang for urinating
second visit: informal for defecating
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Two trips to the toilet and a bout of diarrhoea: a very bad state of affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' looks like more toilet trouble, but it is simply the letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: Piss-poor is vulgar British slang for extremely poor in quality, so it means very bad.

clue.text: 23 Mars trips taking in Earth

indicators.note: taking something in means letting it enter, so one piece is added inside
trips as in stumbles suggests the letters lose their footing and fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for earth, as on electrical plugs

explanation.surface: Space missions to Mars that also stop off on Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is the answer at 23-down, MARK, used here as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A smear is a dirty streak or stain, which is a kind of mark.

clue.text: Wife always shows style

parts.note: w is the abbreviation for wife, as in genealogies
ay or aye is an old word for always or ever; that the answer also sits inside this word is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A wife who is never anything but stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: A way of doing something is a manner or style of doing it.

clue.text: Spectator has neither cold nor hot drink

indicators.note: having neither of two things means both are absent, so they come out of the word

parts.note: a spectator is someone who watches
C for cold and H for hot, as on taps; both are removed

explanation.surface: A spectator has a drink that is neither cold nor hot: lukewarm, presumably.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes cold and hot describe the drink; they are tap letters to strip out of the spectator.
explanation.definitionFit: Water is the most basic drink of all, so it is defined by an example of its use.

clue.text: One before 24, note

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Gospel that comes just before the answer at 24-across in the New Testament
second meaning: to notice or pay attention to something

explanation.walkthrough: 24 is LUKE, the third Gospel; the Gospel just before it in the Bible gives one meaning, and taking note gives the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark is the second Gospel, directly preceding Luke, and to mark something is to note or heed it.

clue.text: Large and small guitar book

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
uke is short for ukulele, a small four-stringed guitar

explanation.surface: Big and little guitars described in one book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large and small' looks like a size pairing; only Large gives a letter and 'small guitar' is the ukulele.
explanation.definitionFit: Luke is one of the four Gospels, a book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Get wicked vagrant dog to bathe

indicators.note: a vagrant wanders without fixed place, so these letters roam into a new order

parts.note: these ten letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to fetch a scruffy stray dog for its bath.
explanation.walkthrough: Vagrant looks like it describes the dog, but it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to the bad is an idiom meaning to fall into moral ruin, so it means to become wicked.

clue.text: Retired Parisian perhaps with no capital cut costs

indicators.note: having no capital means losing the head, so the word gives up its first letter

parts.note: ret is the abbreviation for retired
someone from Paris is French; the first letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A retired Parisian, now living outside the capital, has to economise.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital suggests Paris itself, but here it means the capital, or initial, letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrench is to reduce spending, especially in response to financial difficulty, which is cutting costs.

clue.text: American on canvas heard "Fury, by knockout"

indicators.note: heard means we go by the sound of the word that follows, not its spelling

parts.note: wrath means fury, and in British speech it is said with a short o
KO is the standard abbreviation for a knockout

explanation.surface: A boxing report: a US fighter on the canvas, the crowd hearing fury at the knockout.
explanation.walkthrough: On canvas suggests a floored boxer, but means a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Rothko was an American abstract expressionist painter famous for large canvases of colour fields.
